This patch disables sparse attention via an environment variable to force dense attention computation on architectures that do not support FlashMLA.




## Purpose

Blackwell RTX 6000 Pro is sm120 and is not supported by FlashMLA, so none of the models that use DSA will run. This includes Deepseek Exp, 3.2 and GLM 5+.

## Test Plan

Run:

VLLM_MLA_FORCE_DENSE=1 vllm serve koushd/GLM-5.1-NVFP4 -tp 8 

## Test Result

Model loads and performs inference correctly, whereas it would crash on load before.

With this patch the following end up being used for attention computation:

The PyTorch fallback for fp8_mqa_logits / fp8_paged_mqa_logits added in
the previous commit for SM80 compatibility uses Python-level nested
loops, which also activates on GB10/SM121 (DGX Spark) since DeepGEMM
requires SM90 or SM100. A user reported ~5 t/s running GLM-5.1 on an
8-node DGX Spark cluster due to this.

Micro-benchmark on GB10 (before this patch):
  fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch (ctx=2048):  10.05 ms/call
  fp8_mqa_logits_torch (M=N=2048):        11.46 ms/call

Adds two Triton kernels matching DeepGEMM's signatures:
  - fp8_paged_mqa_logits_triton (decode)
  - fp8_mqa_logits_triton (prefill)

Both dequant FP8 on-the-fly, compute Q@K^T, apply relu + per-head
weights, and sum across heads in a single kernel launch.

Benchmark after this patch:
  fp8_paged_mqa_logits_triton (ctx=2048):  0.09 ms/call (105x faster)
  fp8_mqa_logits_triton (M=N=2048):        0.54 ms/call (21x faster)

At ctx=2048 across 60 sparse layers, this saves ~597 ms/token,
projecting 5 t/s -> ~30+ t/s on DGX Spark.

The PyTorch implementations remain in mqa_logits_fallback.py as
correctness references for tests.

The PyTorch fallback for fp8_mqa_logits / fp8_paged_mqa_logits added in
the previous commit for SM80 compatibility uses Python-level nested
loops, which also activates on GB10/SM121 (DGX Spark) since DeepGEMM
requires SM90 or SM100. A user reported ~5 t/s running GLM-5.1 on an
8-node DGX Spark cluster due to this.

Micro-benchmark on GB10 (before this patch):
  fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch (ctx=2048):  10.05 ms/call
  fp8_mqa_logits_torch (M=N=2048):        11.46 ms/call

Adds two Triton kernels matching DeepGEMM's signatures:
  - fp8_paged_mqa_logits_triton (decode)
  - fp8_mqa_logits_triton (prefill)

Both dequant FP8 on-the-fly, compute Q@K^T, apply relu + per-head
weights, and sum across heads in a single kernel launch.

Benchmark after this patch:
  fp8_paged_mqa_logits_triton (ctx=2048):  0.09 ms/call (105x faster)
  fp8_mqa_logits_triton (M=N=2048):        0.54 ms/call (21x faster)

At ctx=2048 across 60 sparse layers, this saves ~597 ms/token,
projecting 5 t/s -> ~30+ t/s on DGX Spark.

The PyTorch implementations remain in mqa_logits_fallback.py as
correctness references for tests.

Stock vLLM 0.23 plus Transformers 5.11 resolves `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, then fails backend selection because sparse MLA has no compatible backend. A focused port of this PR's environment flag, `is_v32` guards, and `indexer.*` weight skip selects `TRITON_MLA` and loads the model.

That exposed one additional blocker during first token generation:

```text
ValueError: Head dimension 192 is not supported by MLA.
```

`MLACommonMetadata.__post_init__` validates through `MLACommonBackend`, whose accepted sizes are `[320, 576]`, even though `TritonMLABackend.get_supported_head_sizes()` returns `[]` to accept arbitrary dimensions. This checkpoint's compressed KV head is `kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim = 128 + 64 = 192`.

Adding `192` to the common metadata whitelist made direct vLLM generation succeed. Short-prompt output matched Transformers generation. The same patched vLLM then completed:

- two SkyRL BF16 LoRA GRPO steps with nonzero advantages, gradients, optimizer updates, and post-update adapter sync
- one SkyRL NF4 QLoRA GRPO step with absolute advantage `0.7071`, gradient norm `0.0449`, and post-update adapter sync

Current vLLM 0.26 native SM120 sparse MLA still rejects this tiny checkpoint because its sparse backend supports head size 576 only. Dense fallback remains useful for development. At smoke-test sequence lengths below this model's `index_topk=2048`, dense attention covers the same complete prefix; this does not claim long-context DSA equivalence.

Suggested follow-up in this PR: accept 192 in common MLA metadata or make metadata validation use selected backend's head-size contract. PR also needs rebase because GitHub currently reports merge conflicts.

- `VLLM_MLA_FORCE_DENSE=1`, `enable_prefix_caching=false`, and `enable_chunked_prefill=false` completed 200/200 SkyRL GRPO QLoRA updates for `inference-optimization/GLM-5.2-0.8B-A0.8B`. Run exited 0 after 16 minutes of training.
- Switched from noisy text reward to a balanced 12-case symbolic boolean truth-table task. Prompts contain only `0`, `1`, `&`, `|`, `^`, and `=`. Rollouts are constrained to checkpoint token IDs 15/16 (`0`/`1`), removing English-comprehension dependence.
- Deterministic exact-match eval improved from 50% at step 0 to 83.3% at steps 40/60, fluctuated through 66.7-83.3%, then reached 91.7% at steps 160, 180, and 200. Full series: `50.0, 50.0, 83.3, 83.3, 66.7, 75.0, 75.0, 83.3, 91.7, 91.7, 91.7` at steps `0,20,...,200`.
- Mean sampled reward rose from 0.4875 over first 20 updates to 0.7750 over last 20. GRPO produced nonzero advantages and gradients on 179/200 updates; zero-gradient updates corresponded to groups where every sample received same reward. Mean grad norm was 3.1322, range 0-7.3125. Every update completed LoRA sync back to vLLM.
- Prefix caching disabled alone is insufficient for 192-wide head. Both structured-output and `allowed_token_ids` one-token rollouts crashed first generation while chunked prefill remained enabled. Root failure remained `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache only support the head_dim to 320 or 576`. Disabling chunked prefill avoided compressed-cache gather path.

This validates exact model through repeated dense-fallback rollout, reward, GRPO advantage, QLoRA backward/update, and adapter-sync cycles, with clear learning signal. It does not validate 192-head compressed-cache gather or MTP. Current compatibility recipe needs all three settings above.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces the VLLM_MLA_FORCE_DENSE environment variable to allow forcing dense attention and disabling the sparse attention indexer, which is useful for architectures where DeepGEMM is unsupported. Additionally, it replaces has_deep_gemm() with is_deep_gemm_supported() throughout the codebase to ensure better compatibility checks. Feedback was provided to improve the robustness of weight loading in the DeepSeek-V2 model by checking the model's internal state rather than the environment variable directly.
